span.p:
1 · CURATE
you, in Zotero
A handful of grounding papers is
enough. Breadth buys you
very little in this genre.
papers/bibliography.bib

div.style: color: rgb(30, 27, 75) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
color: rgb(51, 65, 85) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
ENRICHMENT — not worth it here
docling · embed · bertopic
Neither SKILL.md mentions embed_index.
Both use src.retrieval.search() — BM25, stdlib —
and building a semantic index to place four
citations is effort spent in the wrong place.
render is the drafting layer's own publish step
python -m src.draft render — it was never
enrichment work, and stopped being a stage in 4.0.0

div.style: color: rgb(5, 46, 22) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
3 · DRAFT
mostly original content
tutorial-writer — one path, keyboard-first,
verified to actually run. Citations are
banned mid-lesson; they live only in
a closing “Where to go next”.
textbook-chapter-writer — objectives,
worked examples, exercises. Cites for
motivation and background only.
content/drafts/<slug>.md

div.style: color: rgb(69, 10, 10) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

p.small:
May legitimately pass with
zero citations. Both SKILL.md
files say so explicitly — this is
the one genre where an empty
reference list is correct.

div.style: color: rgb(69, 10, 10) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

p.small:
drop the claim; the lesson
rarely needed it in the first place

div.style: color: rgb(59, 7, 100) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

p.small:
tutorial-writer passes
--heading "Further reading",
which then survives into the render
instead of being stripped

div.style: color: rgb(66, 32, 6) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

p.b: the real failure mode here isn't a bad citekey
p.small:
It is writing the wrong genre: a tutorial that explains
instead of instructing, or a chapter that instructs instead
of explaining. Both SKILL.md files open by warning about
exactly that — and no gate in this repository can catch it.
You are the check.

svg.text: Genre B — teaching writers: tutorial-writer, textbook-chapter-writer
